chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not scrutinize the people, lest you remain without a friend.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of constantly scrutinizing others according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the chapter on 'The Overlooking of Faults' (Al-I'tiraf bi al-Dhunun), Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the social consequence of excessive scrutiny, warning that a habit of searching for others' defects inevitably leads to personal isolation. This hadith underscores the Shia ethical principle of 'good opinion' (Husn al-Zann), suggesting that preserving communal bonds requires overlooking minor flaws rather than dissecting them.
